tob_fiddler.text: We start slow, so everyone can find the tune, then we speed up until somebody falls off. Come back on a Friday, and bring your ears and your dancing shoes.
In Gaelic a cèilidh was a visit first: songs and stories round a neighbour's fire. The dancing came later, and so did the falling off.

tob_barman.text: Whisky's from just up the hill, the cheese is from just out of town, and the fish is from just off the pier. It's a short menu, and a good one.
Is toil leam iasg: I like fish. Cha toil leam ice in a good malt. You learn a lot of Gaelic from a barman's opinions.
